extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for who may be the applicant on a U.S. patent application (including joint inventors, assignees, persons with proprietary interest), procedures for changing or correcting the applicant/name, title requirements, and fees (filing, size, excess claims, non-electronic). Covers timing, required documents, petitions, and fee allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence of ownership for 37 CFR 1.46 applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is the assignee or a person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention, documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment for an assignee, employment agreement for a person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention) should be recorded as provided for in part 3 of this chapter no later than the date the issue fee is paid in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record evidence in accordance with 37 CFR part 3 no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for applicants showing sufficient proprietary interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter, such applicant must submit a petition including: (i) the fee set forth in § 1.17(g); (ii) a showing that such person has sufficient proprietary interest in the matter; and (iii) a statement that making the application for patent by a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter on behalf of and as agent for the inventor is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 409.05 for discussion of evidence necessary to show sufficient proprietary interest. The Office may publish notice of the filing in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.46(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or update of applicant name (application data sheet required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant under this section must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the correct or updated name of the applicant in the applicant information section (§ 1.76(b)(7)) in accordance with § 1.76(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no change in applicant but only name correction, submit ADS specifying corrected/updated name with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for removals per § 1.76(c)(2). A change recorded pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 16(1)(ii) will change the applicant name in a nonprovisional international design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of applicant after an original applicant specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to change the applicant under this section after an original applicant has been specified must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the applicant in the applicant information section and comply with §§ 3.71 and 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a change of applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 occurs (e.g., from inventor to assignee), the new applicant must establish ownership of the application under 37 CFR 3.71(b) and 3.73. A request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2) should not be filed after the patent has issued because such a request cannot be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirement despite assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the whole or a part interest in the invention or in the patent to be issued is assigned or obligated to be assigned, an oath or declaration must be executed by the actual inventor or each actual joint inventor, except as provided for in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.64 concerning execution of a substitute statement by an assignee, obligated assignee, or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grant to real party in interest and notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is granted on an application filed under this section by a person other than the inventor, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest. Where a real party in interest has filed an application under 37 CFR 1.46, the applicant shall notify the Office of any change in the real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee; the Office will treat absence of such a notice as indication of no change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of real party in interest (e.g., using box 3 of PTOL-85B) will not change the applicant of record unless a proper request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 is filed no later than payment of the issue fee. Example: issued patent may identify Assignee X as applicant and Assignee Y as assignee if ownership changed and only box 3 was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default applicant when no applicant is identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no applicant is identified, the Office will, by default, consider the inventor to be the applicant (e.g., to complete processing of the application so that it can be forwarded for examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request to change the applicant must include an ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 and comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73. New applicant must establish ownership under 3.71(b) and 3.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of incorrectly named applicant (petition under 1.182 required)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1) does not provide for deletion of a party who was incorrectly named as the applicant. In such a situation, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182, including the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f), may be filed and accompanied by an ADS specifying the correct name of the applicant in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should provide an adequate explanation regarding the identification of a party as the applicant who was not the actual applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor typographical correction of 1.46 applicant name before issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If a minor typographical error in a 37 CFR 1.46 applicant's name is detected prior to payment of the issue fee, a request to correct the applicant's name under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1) should be filed promptly and must be filed no later than payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request may be a signed transmittal letter filed with an ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the correct name and shown with appropriate markings (underlining for additions, strikethrough for deletions). The request should clearly indicate it is filed under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1). Neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(c) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant name after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the minor typographical error in the applicant’s name is not detected until after the payment of the issue fee, the application must be withdrawn from issue or a certificate of correction must be filed, because amendments are not permitted after the payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawn from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c)(2), the request to correct the applicant's name under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1) must be submitted with an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 for utility/plant applications. For design applications, petition to withdraw under 1.313(c)(3) and request under 1.46(c)(1) should be accompanied by a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d). If a certificate of correction is filed after patent issues, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 must accompany it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name-change updates for 1.46 applicants (entity renaming)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 37 CFR 1.46 applicant’s name changes (e.g., XYZ, LLC changes its name to XYZ, Inc.), a request to update the name of the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(1) should be filed promptly and must be filed no later than payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request may be a signed transmittal letter filed with an ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the correct name with appropriate markings. Neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(c) is required, though applicant may submit a 3.73(c) statement referencing the name-change document if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors must apply jointly and make oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply for a patent jointly and each must make the required oath or declaration; neither of them alone, nor less than the entire number, can apply for a patent for an invention invented by them jointly, except as provided in § 1.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors may still be joint applicants even if they did not work together, did not make same type/amount of contribution, or did not contribute to every claim. If a joint inventor refuses to join or cannot be found after diligent effort, other joint inventor(s) may make the application on behalf of themselves and the omitted inventor (35 U.S.C. 116(b)). See MPEP § 409.02 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by legal representative for deceased or incapacitated inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased or under legal incapacity, the legal representative of the inventor may make an application for patent on behalf of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.43 and MPEP § 409.01(a) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention may not exceed 500 characters in length and must be as short and specific as possible. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive and should contain fewer than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless supplied in an ADS (§ 1.76), the title should appear at top of first page of the specification. If the title is not descriptive of the invention claimed, the examiner should require substitution of a new title clearly indicative of the invention (form paragraphs 6.11 and 6.11.01 may be used). If applicant fails to supply satisfactory title, examiner may change title by examiner's amendment at allowance (see MPEP § 1302.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Words not to include at beginning of title
rubrics_metrics.description: The following words are not considered as part of the title of an invention and should not be included at the beginning of the title; they will be deleted when entered into the Office's computer records: 'A', 'An', 'The', 'Improved', 'Improvement(s) in/for/of', 'New', 'Novel', 'Related to', 'Design', 'Design for/of (a)', 'Ornamental design', 'Ornamental'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: 'New' and 'Design' will not be deleted when part of a proper name (e.g., 'New York' or 'Design-aiding apparatus').

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing, search, and examination fees due on filing (timing and surcharges)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) the following fees are required: basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a),(b),(c) or (e)); search fee (1.16(k),(l),(m),(n)); examination fee (1.16(o)-(r)); application size fee (1.16(s)), if applicable; excess claims fees (1.16(h),(i)), if applicable; and non-electronic filing fee (1.16(t)), if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic filing, search and examination fees are due on filing, but may be paid later if paid within time period in 37 CFR 1.53(f) and include surcharge in 37 CFR 1.16(f). Provisional basic filing fee (1.16(d)) due on filing or within 1.53(g) with surcharge. See 37 CFR 1.492 for international national stage fees and MPEP § 1415 for reissue fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee: thresholds, exclusions, and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)) applies to any application whose specification (including claims) and drawings exceed 100 sheets of paper. The fee applies for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof over 100 sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes ASCII/plain text or XML sequence listings or computer program listing appendix submitted on read-only optical disc or via EFS as applicable (see 37 CFR 1.52(f)). Preliminary amendments present on filing date are part of original disclosure and are counted. Office does not recommend filing substitute specifications or multiple sets of drawings. For content on read-only optical disc, each three kilobytes of content is counted as a sheet (37 CFR 1.52(f)(1)). For EFS submissions, paper-equivalent is considered 75% of rendered sheets for computing the fee; sequence listings/program listings in ASCII/XML as associated files may be excluded; PDF/TIFF listings are not excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees (thresholds and calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.16(h) sets forth the excess claims fee for each independent claim in excess of three. 37 CFR 1.16(i) sets forth the excess claims fee for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty. Fees apply regardless of filing date and apply to reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for proper multiple dependent claims calculated based on number of claims to which the multiple dependent claim refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)); a separate fee required in each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim (37 CFR 1.16(j)). For improper multiple dependent claim, fee charged is that for a single dependent claim. For nonprovisional applications filed without claims, if >3 independent claims, >20 total claims, or a multiple dependent claim presented, excess claims fee due when presented. Additional or unpaid claim fees due with an amendment must be paid prior to consideration of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments affecting claims: fee timing and entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of an amendment affecting the claims, payment of fees for those claims in excess of the number previously paid for is required. Amendments before the first action, or not filed in reply to an Office action, presenting additional claims in excess of the number already paid for, not accompanied by the full additional fee due, will not be entered in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment of a claim that changes a dependent claim to an independent claim or that increases number of claims referred to in a multiple dependent claim requires additional fees. Additional fees due with an amendment are calculated on basis of the claims which would be present if the amendment were entered. The additional fees are required prior to any consideration by the examiner. Money paid for a proposed amendment will not be refunded by reason of nonentry; unentered claims will not be counted when calculating fee due in subsequent amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim form correctness and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of determining fees, a claim will be treated as dependent if it contains reference to one or more other claims. Any claim in dependent form that is not a proper dependent claim (e.g., does not include every limitation of the claim on which it depends) will be required to be canceled as not being a proper dependent claim; cancellation of further claims depending on such a claim will likewise be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may amend claims to place them in proper dependent form, or redraft them as independent claims upon payment of any necessary additional fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic filing fee and DOCX nonconformity fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(t)) applies to certain original patent applications not filed by electronic means. For any application filed on or after January 17, 2024 under 35 U.S.C. 111 filed non-electronically, the fee for not conforming to USPTO requirements for submission in DOCX format is also applicable (37 CFR 1.16(u)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.445(a)(1)(ii) for non-electronic filing fee portion of transmittal fee for international applications filed with USPTO as receiving Office on/after November 15, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of an insufficient payment when applicant does not specify allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted for the fees due on filing in a nonprovisional application is insufficient and the applicant has not specified the fees to which the payment is to be applied, the Office will apply the payment in a prescribed order until the payment is expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order begins with (1) the basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a)-(e)); (2) the non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(t)); (additional items follow in the Office's published ordering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) apply to excess claims that are presented during a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607.02 for refund policies and MPEP § 608.01(n) for multiple dependent claim practice.
